keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Kokang was regained by 5 January 2024 and Lashio taken in early August 2024. The state is absent from August 2009 (junta occupation) to the end of 2023.

region.text: Kokang, 'its total land area is around 1,895 square kilometers': a 25 km circle at Laukkai cut to Shan State

ledger.note: 1989: the MNDAA is formed on 12 March by Pheung Kya-shin, the head of the CPB's Kokang branch, 'the first one to sign a ceasefire agreement with the Burmese government'. The page does not give the ceasefire month; the CPB page says the Kokang defections began on 12 March 1989.

region.text: Kokang, 'its total land area is around 1,895 square kilometers': a 25 km circle at Laukkai cut to Shan State

ledger.note: 2009: the Tatmadaw takes Kokang. 'On 24 August, it was occupied by troops of the Tatmadaw, Burma's military junta, led by General Min Aung Hlaing' after the August 2009 clash; the MNDAA page: it 'lost control of Kokang'.

region.text: Kokang, 'its total land area is around 1,895 square kilometers': a 25 km circle at Laukkai cut to Shan State

ledger.note: 2015: the MNDAA tries to retake Kokang. 'On 9 February 2015 the MNDAA tried to retake the area, clashing with Burmese government forces in Laukkai'; President Thein Sein declared martial law in Kokang on 17 February (Laukkai page). The pages give no result.

region.text: Kokang, 'its total land area is around 1,895 square kilometers': a 25 km circle at Laukkai cut to Shan State

ledger.note: 2024: the MNDAA retakes Laukkai. The junta's last outpost before the city, Four Buddhist Statues Hill, fell on 6 December 2023; 'most' of Laukkai was MNDAA by 28 December; 'On 5 January 2024, the MNDAA gained full control of Laukkai' (MNDAA page).

region.text: Kokang, 'its total land area is around 1,895 square kilometers': a 25 km circle at Laukkai cut to Shan State

ledger.note: 2024: the contest over Kokang closes with the fall of Laukkai on 5 January (the pages do not say whether fighting from 2015 to 2023 was continuous).

region.text: Lashio, 'captured by rebel forces in early August 2024': a 30 km circle cut to Shan State

ledger.note: 2024: the MNDAA takes Lashio in early August ('captured by rebel forces in early August 2024'; the Myanmar civil war page: 'On 3 August, the MNDAA captured Lashio'), the largest town in northern Shan State; it withdrew in April 2025 under a ceasefire deal.

notes: Rebel state added by se-04-x; CPB (written here) names it as successor. The state is absent from August 2009 to the end of 2023. The contest opened in February 2015 closes in January 2024; the pages do not say whether fighting was continuous. Lashio's April 2025 withdrawal is outside the dossier's end year (2024). Dates differ: Laukkai 5 January 2024 (MNDAA and Laukkai pages) against 'December 2023' elsewhere; Lashio 'early August 2024' (Lashio page) against 3 August (civil war page); ceasefire of 1989 has no month. Not drawn: the Mong La NDAA and the TNLA and KIA gains of Operation 1027 (Mogok, Gangdau Yang, Namhkam: civil war page, no maps). Belligerent slugs 'ta-ang-national-liberation-army' and 'arakan-army' (the latter written here) name co-belligerents; the TNLA has no dossier. Page budget: 5 pages including coordinate pages.
